input.content:
# -separate-named semantics

Binary: `/workspace/executable` (goimports-reviser v3.0.0-20260303205914-9926ea38658f, built go1.26.0).
All experiments run inside `/tmp/probe/separate-named/*`, each with a `go.mod`
(`module example.com/proj` + `go 1.21`) unless the module name is stated otherwise.
Stdout/stderr captured separately; exit codes recorded.

Log lines on stderr are Go `log` default format: `YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS <msg>` (verified with
`od -c`: bytes are `2 0 2 6 / 0 8 / 1 0   1 4 : 3 5 : 3 1   P a t h s : ...`). Timestamps are
elided as `<TS>` below.

---

## Confirmed behaviors

### C1. Flag help text (exact, from usage dump)

`/workspace/executable -badflag >/dev/null 2>usage.txt` then `grep -A2 separate-named usage.txt | cat -A`:

```
  -separate-named$
    ^IOption will separate named imports from the rest of the imports, per group. Optional parameter.$
```

i.e. two spaces + `-separate-named`, newline, four spaces + TAB + the description.
**This differs from README.md**, which claims the text is
`Separate named imports from their group with a new line. Optional parameter.` and indents the
description with 8 spaces. Trust the binary.

### C2. Boolean flag parsing (stdlib `flag` semantics)

File `t10.go`:
```go
package p

import (
	"fmt" // c1
	"os" // c2
	al "path/filepath" // c3
	b "strings" // c4
)
```

| command | effect |
|---|---|
| `executable -separate-named -output stdout t10.go` | separation ON |
| `executable -separate-named=true -output stdout t10.go` | ON |
| `executable -separate-named=1 -output stdout t10.go` | ON |
| `executable --separate-named -output stdout t10.go` | ON |
| `executable -separate-named=false -output stdout t10.go` | OFF |
| `executable -separate-named=0 -output stdout t10.go` | OFF |
| `executable -separate-named=yes -output stdout t10.go` | usage to stderr, exit 2 (bad bool) |

`executable -separate-named true t6.go` treats `true` as a *target path* (bool flags take no
separate argument):
```
=== EXIT: 1
=== STDERR ===
<TS> Paths: [true t6.go]
<TS> Processing true
<TS> Failed to fix file: open /tmp/probe/separate-named/base/true: no such file or directory
```

### C3. `_` (blank) and `.` (dot) imports DO count as "named"

Input `F1.go` (module `example.com/proj`; `aliased`, `blankstd`, `dotstd` are non-existent paths —
they still resolve to the *general* group because no package loading happens without
`-rm-unused`/`-set-alias`):

```go
package p

import (
	"fmt"
	_ "blankstd"
	. "dotstd"
	al "aliased"
	"github.com/a/plain"
	_ "github.com/b/blank"
	. "github.com/c/dot"
	x "github.com/d/named"
	"os"
)
```

Command: `/workspace/executable -separate-named -output stdout F1.go` → **exit 0**

stdout (`cat -A`, `^I` = TAB, `$` = EOL):
```
package p$
$
import ($
^I"fmt"$
^I"os"$
$
^I"github.com/a/plain"$
$
^Ial "aliased"$
^I_ "blankstd"$
^I. "dotstd"$
^I_ "github.com/b/blank"$
^I. "github.com/c/dot"$
^Ix "github.com/d/named"$
)$
```
stderr:
```
<TS> Paths: [F1.go]
<TS> Processing F1.go
```

Baseline, same file, `/workspace/executable -output stdout F1.go` → exit 0:
```
package p$
$
import ($
^I"fmt"$
^I"os"$
$
^Ial "aliased"$
^I_ "blankstd"$
^I. "dotstd"$
^I"github.com/a/plain"$
^I_ "github.com/b/blank"$
^I. "github.com/c/dot"$
^Ix "github.com/d/named"$
)$
```

Conclusion: `_` and `.` are treated exactly like any other alias — they land in the *named*
sub-block. The general group split into `["github.com/a/plain"]` + blank + all 6 named entries.

### C4. An alias identical to the package's own name still counts as named

`t4.go`:
```go
package p

import (
	slices "golang.org/x/exp/slices"
	"golang.org/x/exp/maps"
	fmt "fmt"
	"os"
	pkg "github.com/x/pkg"
)
```
`/workspace/executable -separate-named -output stdout t4.go` → exit 0:
```go
package p

import (
	"os"

	fmt "fmt"

	"golang.org/x/exp/maps"

	pkg "github.com/x/pkg"
	slices "golang.org/x/exp/slices"
)
```
So "named" == "the `ImportSpec` has a `Name`", *not* "the alias differs from the package name".
No name-vs-path comparison is performed. (`fmt "fmt"` is separated from `"os"` inside the std group.)

### C5. The split is applied per group, to every group

`t8.go` (module `example.com/proj`, dirs `sub1/`, `sub2/` exist):
```go
package p

import (
	"fmt"
	al "os"
	"example.com/proj/sub1"
	ps "example.com/proj/sub2"
	"corp.io/a"
	cs "corp.io/b"
	"github.com/gen/x"
	gs "github.com/gen/y"
)
```

`/workspace/executable -company-prefixes 'corp.io' -output stdout t8.go` → exit 0:
```go
package p

import (
	"fmt"
	al "os"

	"github.com/gen/x"
	gs "github.com/gen/y"

	"corp.io/a"
	cs "corp.io/b"

	"example.com/proj/sub1"
	ps "example.com/proj/sub2"
)
```

`/workspace/executable -company-prefixes 'corp.io' -separate-named -output stdout t8.go` → exit 0:
```go
package p

import (
	"fmt"

	al "os"

	"github.com/gen/x"

	gs "github.com/gen/y"

	"corp.io/a"

	cs "corp.io/b"

	"example.com/proj/sub1"

	ps "example.com/proj/sub2"
)
```
All four groups (std, general, company, project) split independently.

### C6. Named block goes AFTER the unnamed block, separated by exactly one empty line

Empty line contains no whitespace at all. `od -c` of the t5 output shows `... " o s " \n \n \t c ...`
— i.e. `\n\n\t`, never `\n\t\n`.

### C7. Sorting inside the named sub-block is by IMPORT PATH (byte-wise), not by alias

`t11.go`:
```go
package p

import (
	z "github.com/a/Zeta"
	a "github.com/a/alpha"
	B "github.com/a/Beta"
	c "github.com/a/_under"
	d "github.com/a/beta"
)
```
`/workspace/executable -separate-named -output stdout t11.go` → exit 0:
```go
package p

import (
	B "github.com/a/Beta"
	z "github.com/a/Zeta"
	c "github.com/a/_under"
	a "github.com/a/alpha"
	d "github.com/a/beta"
)
```
Order is `Beta` < `Zeta` < `_under` < `alpha` < `beta` — plain byte comparison
(`'B'`=0x42 < `'Z'`=0x5A < `'_'`=0x5F < `'a'`=0x61 < `'b'`=0x62). No case folding, no locale.

`n1.go` proves the alias *kind* is irrelevant to the ordering:
```go
package p

import (
	. "github.com/zzz/z"
	_ "github.com/aaa/a"
	x "github.com/mmm/m"
	"github.com/nnn/n"
)
```
→

## Exact strings / formats

Nothing is printed by `-separate-named` itself. Only the normal per-run log lines appear:


Usage entry, byte-exact (`\t` shown literally):

```
  -separate-named
    \tOption will separate named imports from the rest of the imports, per group. Optional parameter.
```

Emitted separator inside the import block: a single `\n` producing a completely empty line
(no tab, no space). Import lines are `\t` + optional `<alias> ` + `"<path>"`.

## Algorithm inference

```
INPUT:  specs      = []ImportSpec{Path string, Alias string /* "" if none */, Comment string}
        order      = parsed -imports-order (default std,general,company,project)
        sepNamed   = -separate-named

# 1. (pre-pass, unrelated to this flag) -rm-unused removes specs; -set-alias fills in Alias
#    for versioned paths and for paths whose package name != last path element.
#    => both run BEFORE step 2, so tool-generated aliases count as "named".

# 2. Bucket every spec into exactly one group according to `order`:
#      if "blanked" in order and Alias == "_"  -> blanked
#      elif "dotted" in order and Alias == "." -> dotted
#      elif isStd(Path)                        -> std
#      elif hasCompanyPrefix(Path)             -> company        (only if -company-prefixes set)
#      elif isProject(Path)                    -> project
#      else                                    -> general
#    ("blanked"/"dotted" win over everything else when present in -imports-order.)

# 3. Sort each group by the tuple (Path, Alias), byte-wise ascending.
#    Unnamed (Alias == "") sorts before every alias for the same Path.
#    NOTE: '.' (0x2E) < 'B' < 'Z' < '_' (0x5F) < 'a'  — plain byte order, no case folding.

# 4. Emit chunks, in the order given by `order`:
chunks = []
for g in order:
    grp = groups[g]
    if grp is empty: continue
    if sepNamed:
        unnamed = [s for s in grp if s.Alias == ""]      # already sorted
        named   = [s for s in grp if s.Alias != ""]      # already sorted
        if unnamed: chunks.append(unnamed)
        if named:   chunks.append(named)
    else:
        chunks.append(grp)

# 5. Render:
text = "import (\n"
     + "\n".join( "\n".join("\t" + render(s) for s in chunk) for chunk in chunks )   # chunks joined by ONE blank line
     + "\n)\n"
   where render(s) = (s.Alias + " " if s.Alias else "") + quote(s.Path) + (" " + s.Comment if any)

# 6. Run go/format (format.Source) over the whole file. This is what column-aligns
#    trailing comments *within each blank-line-delimited run*.
```

Key consequences:
- "Named" == `ImportSpec.Name != nil`. `_`, `.`, and an alias equal to the package name all qualify.
- The named sub-block always follows the unnamed one; there is no way to invert it.
- Empty sub-blocks emit nothing, so you never get two adjacent blank lines, a blank line right
  after `import (`, or a blank line right before `)`.
- Ordering inside the named sub-block is *inherited* from the whole-group path sort — an
  implementation that sorts the group once and then stable-partitions produces identical bytes.
- `blanked` / `dotted` groups are 100 % named, so `-separate-named` is a no-op on them.

## Surprises / gotchas

1. **README's `-separate-named` example is WRONG.** README shows
   ```go
   	extpkg "google.com/golang/pkg"
   	extslice "github.com/PeterRK/slices"
   ```
   The binary emits the reverse (sorted by path, not alias):
   ```
   $ diff -u readme_expected.txt readme_actual.txt
   @@ -6,6 +6,6 @@
    	"github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg"
    	"golang.org/x/exp/slices"

   -	extpkg "google.com/golang/pkg"
    	extslice "github.com/PeterRK/slices"
   +	extpkg "google.com/golang/pkg"
    )
   ```
   Everything else in that README example matches byte-for-byte (verified with
   `/workspace/executable -separate-named -output stdout t1.go`, exit 0, stderr = the two normal log lines).
   The rest of the README example, byte-exact from the binary (`cat -A`):
   ```
   package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata$
   $
   import ($
   ^I"fmt"$
   $
   ^I"github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg"$
   ^I"golang.org/x/exp/slices"$
   $
   ^Iextslice "github.com/PeterRK/slices"$
   ^Iextpkg "google.com/golang/pkg"$
   )$
   ```

2. **README's flag description text is also wrong.** Binary: `Option will separate named imports
   from the rest of the imports, per group. Optional parameter.`

3. **`_` and `.` count as named.** Many people assume "named" means "explicit alias that is a real
   identifier". It does not. With the default `-imports-order` this moves every blank/dot import
   into the tail of its group.

4. **Trailing-comment alignment changes** when the flag is on, because the blank line breaks
   go/printer's alignment run (C15). This is a byte-level difference beyond the blank line itself.

5. **`-use-cache` silently defeats `-separate-named`.** The cache is keyed on file content only,
   not on the flag set. Repro (module `example.com/c2`, `k.go` = `import ("fmt"; al "os")`):
   ```
   $ /workspace/executable -use-cache -output stdout k.go        # exit 0, prints the file unchanged
   $ /workspace/executable -use-cache -separate-named -output stdout k.go
   exit=0   # STDOUT IS EMPTY — no output at all, flag ignored
   $ /workspace/executable -separate-named -output stdout k.go   # exit 0, correct separated output
   ```
   Cache lives at `<os.UserCacheDir>/goimports-reviser/<32-hex-name>` (32-byte files).

6. **Doc comments on import specs are dropped** (both with and without the flag). `t9.go` with
   `// doc for al` above `al "os"` loses that comment entirely. Line (trailing) comments survive
   and are *not* re-spaced (`//x cmt` stays `//x cmt`, it is not normalized to `// x cmt` —
   contradicting the README `-company-prefixes` example).

7. **Duplicate import paths are preserved, not deduplicated** (C8, `t12.go`), and they are split
   across the unnamed/named boundary.

8. `-separate-named true file.go` silently treats `true` as a target path (Go bool-flag semantics),
   producing `Failed to fix file: open <dir>/true: no such file or directory`, exit 1.

9. **Off-dimension but reproducible:** `-rm-unused` stops removing unused imports when the import
   block contains a `_` blank import. Repro in module `example.com/rm2`:
   ```go
   package p
   import (
   	"fmt"
   	unused "strings"
   	_ "net/http/pprof"
   )
   func f() { fmt.Println() }
   ```
   → `unused "strings"` is NOT removed (exit 0). Remove the `_ "net/http/pprof"` line and it IS
   removed. Mention only so a reimplementer does not blame `-separate-named`.

10. The file is written back (mtime updated) even when the content is byte-identical (C16).

---

## Open questions

- Whether the blank-line insertion happens in the generated source text (my inference from C15) or
  via a printer hook cannot be distinguished from the outside; the observable bytes are the same
  under `format.Source` semantics either way.
- I could not construct an input distinguishing sort key `(path, alias)` from `path + " " + alias`;

  < 0x20, which Go identifiers/`_`/`.` cannot.
- Behaviour of `-separate-named` on files with `//go:build` constraints, CRLF line endings, or
  generated-file headers (`-apply-to-generated-files`) was not probed here — expected orthogonal,
  but unverified.
- Whether `-separate-named` affects the `-list-diff` stdout listing rule (it prints the path
  unconditionally in every case I tried, changed or not).

Report: `/tmp/findings/separate-named.md` (1102 lines). Scratch: `/tmp/probe/separate-named/`

DIMENSION: -separate-named

CORE RULE
- "Named" == the ImportSpec has a Name node. `_` and `.` BOTH count as named. An alias equal to the package's own name (`fmt "fmt"`, `slices "golang.org/x/exp/slices"`) also counts — no alias-vs-package-name comparison is done.
- Applied per group, to every group (std, general, company, project) independently.
- Within a group: unnamed block first, then ONE completely empty line (`\n\n\t`, no whitespace), then the named block.
- Sorting is unchanged by the flag: whole group sorted by tuple (path, alias) byte-wise ascending; unnamed (alias "") sorts before any alias for the same path. The flag only stable-partitions that sorted list. So the named sub-block is sorted BY PATH, not by alias.
- Byte order confirmed: '.'(0x2E) < 'B' < 'Z' < '_'(0x5F) < 'a'. No case folding.
- Empty sub-blocks emit nothing ⇒ never two adjacent blank lines, never a blank right after `import (` or before `)`.

INTERACTIONS
- `blanked`/`dotted` groups in -imports-order are 100% named ⇒ flag is a no-op on them (no leading blank). If only `blanked` is in the order, dot imports stay in std/general and DO get pushed into those groups' named blocks (and vice versa).
- -set-alias runs BEFORE grouping ⇒ aliases the tool adds get separated. -set-alias never strips an existing alias.
- -rm-unused runs before separation; all of -rm-unused/-set-alias/-format/-separate-named compose.
- -set-exit-status correctly returns 1 when only the separation is missing; returns 0 on an already-separated file.
- Idempotent (verified md5 stable over 3 runs, both default and blanked/dotted orders).

TOP GOTCHAS
1. README's -separate-named example is WRONG. It shows `extpkg "google.com/golang/pkg"` before `extslice "github.com/PeterRK/slices"`. Binary emits extslice first (path sort). Everything else in that example matches byte-for-byte.
2. README's flag help text is wrong. Binary usage line is exactly:
   `  -separate-named` / `    <TAB>Option will separate named imports from the rest of the imports, per group. Optional parameter.`
3. Comment alignment changes: the inserted blank line breaks go/printer's alignment run, so trailing-comment padding is computed per sub-block. `"fmt" // c1` / `"os"  // c2` (2 cols) vs the un-separated `"fmt"              // c1` (aligned to `al "path/filepath"`). Reimplementation must insert the blank line into the source text before format.Source.
4. -use-cache silently defeats -separate-named: cache is keyed on file content only, not flags. Second run prints NOTHING to stdout even with `-output stdout`. Cache at `<os.UserCacheDir>/goimports-reviser/<32-hex>`.
5. Duplicate import paths are preserved (not deduped) and are split across the unnamed/named boundary.
6. Doc comments above import specs are dropped (flag-independent); trailing `//x cmt` is NOT re-spaced.

FLAG PARSING
- `-separate-named`, `=true`, `=1`, `--separate-named` all enable; `=false`/`=0` disable; `=yes` ⇒ usage to stderr, exit 2. `-separate-named true f.go` treats `true` as a target path ⇒ `Paths: [true f.go]`, `Failed to fix file: open <dir>/true: no such file or directory`, exit 1.

DEGENERATE
- `import ()` ⇒ output is exactly `package p\n`. `import "C"` in its own decl is left untouched; only the parenthesized block is reorganized. Separate single-import decls are merged into one block.
